newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers say drought already cut grain yield.
newsitem.headline: French farmers say drought already cut grain yield.

text.p: France's largest farm union FNSEA said on Tuesday that nearly four months of drought has done irreversible damage to soft winter wheat and barley crops.

Heavy rain since the last week of April helped revive parched crops, but came too late to limit yield losses already estimated at some 20 percent for soft winter wheat and barley, an official from the FNSEA's so-called drought team told Reuters.
"For straw-based cereals, mainly wheat and barley, the yield loss is already of up to 20 percent because of the drought," Jean Doube said.
The situation might, however, vary greatly among regions, he said, adding that it was too early to say how recent rains might help to improve crop potential.
"For 80 percent (of the yield potential) there can be a recovery. For these 80 percent we are saying that the situation is not dramatic if it keeps raining normally until June," he said.
FNSEA officials were cautious over future crop prospects, saying it was too early to choose between the two scenarios they have built.
Under one of these, the drought would persist and grain yields fall further, while under a less pessimistic scenario normal rainfall until June would help limit yield damages.
State weather service Meteo France has said that an average 60 millimetres of rain had hit France since the last week of April, about an entire month's rainfall for May.
Last week government sources said that, except for durum wheat in the south, France was still looking at a good harvest for cereals in 1997.
They said that if it kept raining yields might not reach last year's records but the crop might come close to last year's volume because area was up three percent.
Last year's grain crop was a record 62.46 million tonnes, including 34.69 million tonnes of wheat.
